newsitem.title: CHINA: Statue of Deng to 'see' HK handover - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Statue of Deng to 'see' HK handover - newspaper.

text.p: A six-metre (20-ft) statue of China's late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping will be unveiled before the British colony of Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule on July 1, the Bejing Youth Daily said on Monday.
The statue would "tower over" a coastal city that Deng once visited and "see" Hong Kong's handover, newspaper said.
It did not name the city, but the statue was expected to be erected in southern Shenzhen, neighbouring Hong Kong.
Deng died in Beijing on February 19 at the age of 92.
The newspaper splashed a photograph of the statue on its front page, which showed Deng posing as if moving forward in mid-stride and with a half-smile on his face.
The massive figure was being carved by Bai Lansheng, who sculpted statues of the late Chairman Mao Zedong and premier Zhou Enlai, at a museum in Beijing. The clay model will be cast in bronze later.

Such a monument to Deng would have been impossible in the lifetime of the diminutive revolutionary, whose reforms created a fledgling economic superpower but who abhorred the personality cult that surrounded his predecessor Mao.
